beats.goal: When the Council abandons Wyrmwood, Captain Caelan Rooke defies the evacuation order to recover stranded villagers; Bryn Fen appears to drive storm and cattle toward one ford, while Mira Sedge plants the Council’s genuine seal on a captured wagon.
beats.conflict: Flooded roads, military prohibition, and Rooke’s duty to the boy king war with his duty to the border people.
beats.outcome: Rooke saves most villagers at severe cost, wins the field, and carries the planted seal home convinced that events favor his ambition.

beats.goal: Rooke meets Mira, Nessa, and Bryn at a ruined moor shrine, where they stage a prophecy that mercy will raise him, the Council’s hand will cast him down, and an ash crown will come when he trusts only his own blood.
beats.conflict: Rooke demands certainty; Mira can stage signs, Nessa can alter records, and Bryn can steer weather and roads, but none can compel his choices.
beats.outcome: He refuses an explicit bargain but takes a blackthorn token, returns in triumph, and begins treating his own successes as divine selection.

beats.goal: At the royal capital, Nessa changes one word in a Council annex, turning a phased evacuation into permission for raiders to seize the border depots and uses Mira’s stolen seal to make the document damning.
beats.conflict: Rooke’s sister urges investigation, but frightened soldiers and hungry families demand immediate action.
beats.outcome: Rooke intercepts and confiscates a royal grain convoy, imprisons its courier, and gains a civilian reputation while beginning his first major betrayal.

beats.goal: As famine spreads, the Council sends young King Lestan to a southern stronghold and requires Rooke to surrender his emergency seals and evidence.
beats.conflict: Rooke can obey and preserve his loyalty, or exploit the king’s absence and rule in his name.
beats.outcome: After Bryn delays the escort and Nessa spreads reports of royal betrayal, Rooke lets Lestan depart, reclaims the grain, and accepts the emergency title of Protector.

beats.goal: When the southern convoy misses its expected return, the border lords gather to choose a Protector; Rooke’s sister offers proof that Lestan is safe, but Rooke claims the king has been taken by traitors.
beats.conflict: Accepting the regalia requires him to knowingly deny the truth and transform a temporary defense into personal rule.
beats.outcome: The lords acclaim Rooke as Protector; his apparent rescue of the realm becomes the first political condition he manufactures himself.

beats.goal: Rebel villages shelter raiders, so Nessa alters tax rolls and Mira plants rebel marks while Bryn exposes dry routes; Rooke issues the Bare March decree to burn supplies and destroy suspected settlements.
beats.conflict: Soldiers request a narrower defense, while villages plead for time even though some harbor genuine rebels.
beats.outcome: Rooke defeats the raiders but executes hostages and scorches the land; the border lords offer him kingship, and he accepts a crown of charred heather.

beats.goal: King Lestan returns with Chancellor Maelin, loyal border troops, and the Council’s original annex proving that only Nessa’s alteration made the surrender order criminal.
beats.conflict: Rooke can restore legitimacy by releasing his prisoners and surrendering the crown, or preserve his rule by destroying every witness.
beats.outcome: He burns the records, executes the courier, imprisons Maelin and his sister, and orders no quarter, causing his army and the countryside to abandon him.

beats.goal: Cornered outside the capital, Rooke confronts the three witches as Mira, Nessa, and Bryn each reveal their intervention and his sister proves the Council’s original plan intended to preserve the March.
beats.conflict: He must admit that their signs merely prepared choices he made, or preserve the identity of the king destiny supposedly chose.
beats.outcome: Rooke admits they built the road but not the journey, rejects surrender, and marches after Lestan with his last troops as Bryn’s storm scatters his army.

beats.goal: At the drowned stones of Wyrmwood Moor, Rooke’s final guard confronts Lestan, an army of civilians, and the witches fully manifested through peat-fire, altered voices, and the returning dead.
beats.conflict: Rooke can lay down his sword and spare the living, or order the last volley and seal the causeway to preserve his claim.
beats.outcome: He orders fire, his soldiers refuse, and the uprising captures him; the witches reveal that every prophecy was fulfilled by his choices: “We sow no seed, yet harvest every soul.”

beats.goal: After a public trial, Lestan must decide whether to execute the soldier who became his rival while restoring the government Rooke destroyed.
beats.conflict: Rooke insists the crown made him king; his sister asks what became of the kingdom he claims to have saved.
beats.outcome: Rooke recognizes that he authored his ruin and is hanged by those he wronged; Lestan restores a shared council, honors the victims, and the vanished witches leave only the moor tolling around his unmarked grave.
